xtmux-kua.description:
## PROBLEM

tests/contracts/fresh-db.test.ts asserts that `audit --json` on a virgin DB emits no raw SQLiteError. On a machine with many live tmux sessions the command takes 4-5s (measured: 3.9-4.5s on feat/xtmux-j46.6, 4.7-5.2s on main — main is SLOWER, so this is not caused by any j46 change), which drifts across bun's default 5000ms per-test timeout. It then fails as a TIMEOUT, not as an assertion — so the failure message points at SQLite error leakage, which is not what went wrong. That is the worst kind of flake: it accuses the wrong subsystem.

Reproduced ~1 in 6 runs locally with ~10 live sessions. CI has a near-empty tmux server and has never hit it.

## SCOPE

tests/contracts/fresh-db.test.ts; possibly bin/tmux-session-picker audit (the walk itself).

## SUCCESS

Either the audit walk is fast enough that the assertion is what decides the test, or the test gets an explicit timeout with a comment saying WHY audit is slow (it is O(live panes), unlike its table-mates). A bare timeout bump with no explanation just moves the cliff.

## NON_GOALS
- Rewriting the audit command for performance (separate concern unless the walk turns out to be accidentally quadratic — worth one look).

## CONSTRAINTS
- The test must still fail if audit genuinely leaks a SQLiteError / 'no such table'. Do not weaken the assertion to fix the timing.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] 20 consecutive runs green on a tmux server with 10+ sessions.
- [ ] The SQLite-leak assertion still fails when migrate() is skipped (prove it stayed load-bearing).

## OUTPUT
Root cause (slow walk vs too-tight timeout), the fix, and the 20-run evidence.
xtmux-kua.title: Flaky: fresh-db 'audit never leaks a raw SQLite error' fails as a 5s TIMEOUT on a busy tmux server
